messages.text: wait, did you mean the background particles too? if so, svg is definitely not going to cut it for that.
yes?? i was thinking tiny floating dots... like 200 of them. i don't know why i said svg. brain is fried 🫠
use a single fixed-size canvas for the particles layer behind the svg. just one context, no resizing logic.
oh! that actually makes way more sense than drawing 200 svgs. i was about to write a resize handler for each dot and then hate myself.
also check window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'). if it's true, just render static positions. don't animate at all.
adding that to the checklist. mei mentioned the turquoise theme in her sketch - is that the primary token or a secondary accent? i want to make sure the particles aren't too loud against it.
primary. but for particles, use like 10% opacity turquoise on a dark background. subtle. if it looks like a screensaver, you've failed.
hahaha ok. 'subtle' is my goal, 'vibrating neon disco' is my history.
also pause the rAF loop when document.visibilityState is hidden. don't burn battery on a background tab.
noted. i'll add a visibilitychange listener. this is actually going to be cleaner than i thought. thanks for not letting me use 200 divs with css animations 😅
css animations on 200 elements would tank the main thread. canvas offloads it to the compositor. trust me.
i trust you! mostly because you're right about everything and it's annoying. sending gif in 10 mins if i survive.
keep the wobbly boundaries on the svg layer, though. canvas is just for the dust. don't mix them or z-indexing will ruin your day.
z-index... right. ok. going to code now. 🚀
